messages:
tian: quick heads-up — new int8 bring-up for orpheus-7b shows a subtle regression on KR/ZH suffixes, mostly polite endings and aspect particles. not catastrophic, but visible in our suffix-preservation metric.

maria: oh interesting. is this after the kernel remap + prefix cache change?

lee: yep remap + changed rounding in matmul kernel. saw perf win but didnt expect locale regressions. can you paste an example?

 tian: repro snippet:
 ```
# prompt: translate -> en
KR input: "저는 오늘 학교에 갔습니다."
FP16 output: "I went to school today."
INT8 output: "I went to school today"  <-- missing trailing period sometimes + polite suffix phrasing flattened

ZH input: "我已经吃完了。"
FP16: "I have already eaten."
INT8: "I already ate"  <-- aspect particle nuance lost
```

sanjay: aha that looks like detokenization/piece-level merge stuff — punctuation and final particles get dropped or merged into previous token and then omitted by sampling. could be tokenizer boundary shifts after quantized embedding weighting change.

lee: reproducing locally now on staging-int8. planning to run the suffix-preservation eval (custom metric we use) across our en-kr, en-zh dev sets. will report chrF/BLEU deltas too.

 eval-bot: automated run queued: run_id=run_2026_03_18_042. metrics snapshot: en-kr chrF -0.9, BLEU -0.3, suffix-preservation -3.1 pts; en-zh chrF -0.6, suffix-preservation -2.7 pts. (baseline=fp16_orpheus_7b)

maria: thanks. can you also run with tokenizer v0.13 (old) vs v0.15 (new)? want to know if tokenizer changes + kernel remap interact.

lee: good call — starting that A/B now. also toggling prefix-cache off to isolate KV behavior.

josh: FYI from infra: if we need to rollback remap we should gate it behind a feature flag per cluster. deploy-bot can flip config without redeploy.

tian: thanks — if this reproduces, we'd prefer a narrow rollback on region-staging while we bisect. we want to avoid wide rollback since perf regression matters for tail latency.

maria: quick triage plan: 1) run tokenizer A/B, 2) run kernel remap off/on, 3) run sampling temperature sweep to see if output difference is post-softmax noise, 4) bisect commits between quant-kernel PRs.

sanjay: I'll take bisect (3-4). grabbing a minimal test harness for suffix-preservation metric so runs are cheap. want targeted sentences focusing on polite endings, aspect particles, and sentence-final punctuation.

lee: A/B results coming in: tokenizer diff accounts for ~0.8 pts of the suffix-preservation gap on KR, kernel remap accounts for ~1.9 pts. combined they match eval-bot numbers.

 eval-bot: attach: https://internal.eval/reports/run_2026_03_18_042 (small sample + scatter plots).

maria: ok that points to an interaction. two follow-ups: (a) patch tokenizer to preserve boundary for final-suffix grapheme clusters, (b) adjust remap rounding to match previous fp16 weight scaling.

lee: will prototype tokenizer soft-fix (preserve trailing Josa tokens) and run smoke.

josh: if we land a kernel tweak, can we ship it behind a runtime flag so Dedicated customers unaffected until validated?

 tian: yes please. priority: avoid user-facing quality regressions. let's gate kernel change by default off for production clusters, enable in canary only.

maria: sanjay — once you have the minimal harness, run on the full en-kr dev (~4k sentences) and share the failing subset. will create a ticket to track fix and regression test.

sanjay: on it. ETA today EOD. I'll drop failing examples here and add to the onboarding checklist so future quant bring-ups run suffix-preservation check.

lee: thanks — I'll push tokenizer patch to a feature branch and link PR when ready.

tian: really appreciate the quick turnaround. cc @eng-ml for visibility. :thumbsup:
